lessons.name: IEEE ICRA 2026 (Vienna) and its competitions
lessons.summary: ICRA 2026 was IEEE's robotics research conference in Vienna, with competitions that tested robots on concrete tasks.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

ICRA 2026 was IEEE's robotics research conference in Vienna, with competitions that tested robots on concrete tasks.

![Official ICRA 2026 conference logo](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-ieee-icra-2026-vienna-and-its-competitions.webp)
*Official ICRA 2026 conference logo. Source: [Publisher](https://2026.ieee-icra.org/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Research and demonstrations:** The Vienna edition ran on 1–5 June 2026 at VIECON / Messe Wien, alongside a dedicated competition area.
- **Nine challenges:** Examples included robotic grasping, RoboRacer racing, garment manipulation in LeHome, and legged robots moving over difficult terrain.
- **Software analogy:** Think of each challenge as an integration-test suite: a full robot must complete the task, not merely run one clever function.

> **Key idea:** A competition turns a broad research topic into a task with observable successes and failures.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Pick a tractable slice:** LeHome's garment task gives a concrete reason to study perception and learning, rather than starting with an unrestricted household robot.
- **Read across events:** Compare the research focus with RoboCup German Open, where teams also expose complete systems to shared competition conditions.
- **Worked exercise:** Choose one challenge and write a table of inputs, allowed actions, success conditions, and failure cases before attempting its baseline.

## How to engage

1. **Use the archive:** Watch a conference presentation, then follow the competition directory to that challenge's own technical rules.
2. **Reproduce first:** Run an available baseline and save its configuration, logs, and failed trials before proposing an improvement.
3. **Check the edition:** The Vienna competition has ended; use its materials for learning, not as a current registration invitation.

lessons.name: iREX (International Robot Exhibition)
lessons.summary: iREX is a Japanese exhibition where robot makers show industrial machines, service robots, and the components that make them work.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

iREX is a Japanese exhibition where robot makers show industrial machines, service robots, and the components that make them work.

![Franka Robotics' published preview of its iREX 2025 demonstration](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-irex-international-robot-exhibition.webp)
*Franka Robotics' published preview of its iREX 2025 demonstration. Source: [Publisher](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CvJvWE6kQAw), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Three useful categories:** The official site separates Smart Production Robot, Smart Community Robot, and Component Technologies.
- **Production versus service:** Welding and picking appear alongside cleaning, delivery, and nursing applications; the show is broader than humanoid demonstrations.
- **Software analogy:** Picture a package ecosystem made physical: complete robots are applications, while drives, sensors, and control systems are dependencies.

> **Key idea:** A robot exhibition is most useful when you trace a complete application back to its enabling components.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **See the whole stack:** A software team can inspect how an arm, its tool, sensing, and application fit together rather than treating hardware as a black box.
- **Worked comparison:** Watch Franka Robotics and Agile Robots' 2025 booth videos; list what each demonstration senses, moves, and handles.
- **Compare regions:** ROBOTWORLD offers another Asian exhibition viewpoint, while LogiMAT narrows the focus to warehouse and material-flow applications.

## How to engage

1. **Start remotely:** Use the exhibitor directory to pick a specific application, then read the maker's supporting technical material.
2. **Ask concrete questions:** Request interface documentation and operating constraints for the demonstrated task, not a vague promise that a robot supports AI.
3. **Check names carefully:** The site announces iREX for early December 2027; RoboNext 2026 is a separate event, not the next iREX edition.

lessons.name: KUKA Innovation Award
lessons.summary: The KUKA Innovation Award is a robotics competition that helps selected teams turn research ideas into demonstrations using KUKA equipment.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

The KUKA Innovation Award is a robotics competition that helps selected teams turn research ideas into demonstrations using KUKA equipment.

![KUKA Innovation Award trophies](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-kuka-innovation-award.webp)
*KUKA Innovation Award trophies. Source: [Publisher](https://www.kuka.com/en-de/future-production/research-and-development/kuka-innovation-award), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Research-to-industry competition:** Developers, graduates, and research teams from universities or companies submit ideas addressing a task set by KUKA.
- **Support for finalists:** KUKA lists a supplied robot, training, coaching, and a trade-fair presentation; the winning team receives €20,000.
- **Changing brief:** The 2026 Circular Packaging Challenge concerned packaging's life cycle, including putting products into packaging and recovering packaging for recycling.

> **Key idea:** The valuable constraint is solving a specified application, not simply making an industrial arm move.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Software analogy:** Treat the call like an API contract: an impressive implementation still fails if it does not satisfy the requested behavior.
- **Worked exercise:** Turn one circular-packaging operation into a proposal with an input object, robot action, measurable outcome, and recovery strategy.
- **Prepare progressively:** WorldSkills France offers a complementary view of robot integration: programming is only one part of making an industrial process work.

## How to engage

1. **Read the current call:** Confirm the theme, eligibility, and application process instead of reusing requirements from an older award video.
2. **Study previous finalists:** Identify the problem, robot setup, and evidence each team presented, then compare them with your proposed contribution.
3. **Scope before applying:** Explain what the student team can already demonstrate and which equipment or coaching it would need to complete the application.

lessons.name: LauzHack
lessons.summary: LauzHack is a student-run EPFL hackathon for building team prototypes, not a robotics-only competition.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

LauzHack is a student-run EPFL hackathon for building team prototypes, not a robotics-only competition.

![Published preview of LauzHack 2025](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-lauzhack.webp)
*Published preview of LauzHack 2025. Source: [Publisher](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j1CmyWgrC18), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Build a demonstration:** LauzHack describes hackathons as creativity and prototyping marathons where teams combine existing libraries and interfaces to show an idea.
- **Lausanne setting:** The 2026 edition is scheduled for 21–22 November at EPFL; the official page says applications are closed.
- **Software analogy:** This is closer to shipping a small vertical slice than finishing a production system: demonstrate the essential behavior end to end.

> **Key idea:** A short hackathon rewards a narrow, understandable prototype more than an ambitious robot you cannot demonstrate.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Practice team delivery:** Software students can rehearse the workflow of choosing a problem, integrating tools, and explaining what actually works.
- **Worked project pitch:** Propose a simulated robot sorting objects, with a visible input, decision, and outcome; ask organizers whether it fits the rules.
- **Choose the right venue:** Compare with LeRobot Worldwide Hackathon, whose published challenge materials explicitly focus on robotics and robot-learning demonstrations.

## How to engage

1. **Inspect an archive:** Watch the 2025 event video and read that edition's page to understand the format without confusing past and current arrangements.
2. **Read participation rules:** Check eligibility, team conditions, and what work can be prepared before a future edition.
3. **Ask before transporting hardware:** Confirm whether your proposed robot or simulation is suitable, and do not treat a closed application page as admission.

lessons.name: LeRobot Worldwide Hackathon
lessons.summary: LeRobot Worldwide Hackathon brought online and local teams together to build and share open-source robot-learning demonstrations.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

LeRobot Worldwide Hackathon brought online and local teams together to build and share open-source robot-learning demonstrations.

![Participants at the Paris LeRobot hackathon](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-lerobot-worldwide-hackathon.webp)
*Participants at the Paris LeRobot hackathon. Source: [Publisher](https://42-ai.github.io/posts/LeRobotHackathonHighlights/), CC BY 4.0.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Distributed event:** The published hackathon ran on 14–15 June 2025, with online participation and local sites, including 42 Paris.
- **Shared artifacts:** Submission instructions asked teams for a demonstration video under one minute and the datasets they recorded, when relevant.
- **Robot-learning workflow:** The event introduced the SO-101 and linked LeRobot documentation for recording data and building working demonstrations.

> **Key idea:** A convincing hackathon submission pairs visible robot behavior with the data and code needed to understand it.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Direct local connection:** 42AI's announcement identifies 42, 96 Boulevard Bessières, as the Paris site; this is an existing community link, not a speculative introduction.
- **Software analogy:** Treat the demo as a release and its dataset as a versioned test fixture; both matter when another team investigates the behavior.
- **Worked submission:** Follow the published pattern `[TEAM-N°]-[TEAM NAME]-[DATASET-NAME]` when studying how event datasets were organized.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the kickoff:** Then browse the event organization and the Paris highlights to connect instructions with actual student work.
2. **Reproduce a small task:** With SO-101 and LeRobot, choose one observable behavior before extending it with more ambitious learning.
3. **Use current channels:** Follow official community updates for future opportunities; the June 2025 registration instructions describe an event that has already ended.

lessons.name: LogiMAT
lessons.summary: LogiMAT is a Stuttgart trade fair about moving, storing, and managing goods inside businesses, including warehouse robotics and automation.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

LogiMAT is a Stuttgart trade fair about moving, storing, and managing goods inside businesses, including warehouse robotics and automation.

![Exhibition floor at LogiMAT](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-logimat.webp)
*Exhibition floor at LogiMAT. Source: [Publisher](https://www.logimat-messe.de/en), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Intralogistics:** This means material and information flow inside an organization, from receiving goods through storage, production, and distribution.
- **Process-level view:** The fair connects equipment with software and data handling; it is not a competition to build a single robot.
- **Concrete setting:** The official site advertises 16–18 March 2027 at Stuttgart Trade Fair Centre, with the theme Mind Meets Machine.

> **Key idea:** Warehouse robots only create value when their physical movements fit the surrounding information and material flow.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Software analogy:** Think of a warehouse as a distributed application: moving a box is one operation inside a larger workflow with state and interfaces.
- **Worked visit plan:** Trace one item's route from receipt to dispatch; record where sensing, transport, storage, and software handoffs occur.
- **Compare event scopes:** Robotics & Automation UK (with IntraLogisteX) is another application-focused route into warehouse automation rather than general robotics research.

## How to engage

1. **Learn the vocabulary:** Read the fair profile before watching the machine-vision forum, so its logistics examples have a clear context.
2. **Prepare an interface question:** Ask how a demonstrated solution receives tasks and reports exceptions; distinguish a polished booth sequence from an explained deployment.
3. **Check attendance conditions:** Use the organizer's current dates and visitor information before planning travel; remote talks are a useful first pass.

lessons.name: MACHINA (Station F physical-AI summit)
lessons.summary: MACHINA is a Paris summit about physical AI: applying artificial intelligence to robots and other machines that act in the world.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

MACHINA is a Paris summit about physical AI: applying artificial intelligence to robots and other machines that act in the world.

![Humanoid robot demonstration at MACHINA 2026](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-machina-station-f-physical-ai-summit.webp)
*Humanoid robot demonstration at MACHINA 2026. Source: [Publisher](https://machinasummit.com/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Beyond chat interfaces:** Discussions concern robot intelligence, deployment, and the infrastructure needed to move from prototypes to real applications.
- **Named speakers:** The official 2026 archive includes NVIDIA's Jim Fan and leaders from Google DeepMind, Apptronik, and Hugging Face.
- **Edition distinction:** The inaugural Station F event was in 2026; the current site advertises 7–8 July 2027 at Palais des Congrès.

> **Key idea:** Use a robotics summit to identify testable technical ideas, not to treat every stage prediction as a demonstrated capability.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Software analogy:** A summit is like a technology design review, not an executable benchmark: you still need to inspect the implementation and evidence.
- **Worked listening exercise:** Watch Jim Fan's session and separate three columns: capabilities shown, claims made, and experiments your lab could reproduce.
- **Connect formats:** Mistral AI Robotics Hackathon offers a contrasting hands-on format, where teams must build and pitch a working physical-AI demonstration.

## How to engage

1. **Start with recordings:** Watch the 2026 aftermovie for context, then a technical session before deciding whether the audience matches your goals.
2. **Prepare a precise introduction:** Bring one demonstrated task, a repository, and a concrete technical question rather than requesting an unspecified partnership.
3. **Check current access:** Consult official tickets and program pages; do not assume a summit pass includes a hackathon or robot workshop.

lessons.name: Mistral AI Robotics Hackathon
lessons.summary: Mistral AI Robotics Hackathon was a Paris event combining a physical-AI summit with a 48-hour robot-building sprint.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Mistral AI Robotics Hackathon was a Paris event combining a physical-AI summit with a 48-hour robot-building sprint.

![Published preview of the Mistral AI Robotics and Physical AI Hackathon](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-mistral-ai-robotics-hackathon.webp)
*Published preview of the Mistral AI Robotics and Physical AI Hackathon. Source: [Publisher](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-oA0K_rTBKs), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Specific format:** The published April 11–13 event included a Friday summit and a weekend hackathon, followed by demonstrations and jury pitches.
- **Robot access:** The announcement offered more than 40 robotic arms from Hugging Face's LeRobot team for teams building with Mistral AI.
- **Two settings:** La Maison hosted the summit; Photoroom's offices hosted the build phase, according to the organizer's event listing.

> **Key idea:** The useful result of a robot hackathon is a demonstrated behavior with a clear account of what the team actually built.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Embodied AI:** Here, AI connects to a physical machine rather than producing only text; actions must result in observable behavior.
- **Software analogy:** Build a thin end-to-end feature: input request, model decision, robot action, and visible outcome, rather than several disconnected notebooks.
- **Worked planning exercise:** Sketch a single arm task, divide perception, control, and presentation work, and compare this plan with LeRobot Worldwide Hackathon submissions.

## How to engage

1. **Study the archive:** Watch Entrepreneurs First's event video, then read the published schedule to see how much time was reserved for building.
2. **Read team conditions:** The listing specified teams of five and individual acceptance; do not assume an entire association can register as one participant.
3. **Check future announcements:** This is a past event. Use the public host channel for later opportunities rather than assuming these equipment arrangements recur.

lessons.name: Physical AI Hackathon (Robotics Nation, Helsinki)
lessons.summary: Robotics Nation's Helsinki Physical AI Hackathon challenged teams to automate tasks using paired arms or an arm on a mobile base.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Robotics Nation's Helsinki Physical AI Hackathon challenged teams to automate tasks using paired arms or an arm on a mobile base.

![Two-arm cup-filling demonstration from the Helsinki hackathon project](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-physical-ai-hackathon-robotics-nation-helsinki.webp)
*Two-arm cup-filling demonstration from the Helsinki hackathon project. Source: [Publisher](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NVHb-mLm7kE), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Two hardware tracks:** The listing offered two SO-101 arms working together, or an SO-101 on an omnidirectional LeKiwi platform with Jetson Orin Nano.
- **Short build cycle:** Teams of three to five had 48 hours; the event page lists a €5,000 prize pool and now shows registration closed.
- **Published example:** One team's repository documents two-arm tasks: filling a cup at a tap and placing an object into a cup.

> **Key idea:** Coordinating two arms means learning the relationship between their actions, not just making each arm move independently.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Software analogy:** Treat a two-arm task like cooperating services: one must place the cup where the other expects it before the next action makes sense.
- **Worked behavior:** In the published cup-filling demo, one arm brings the cup while the other operates the tap; both roles define success.
- **Connect the stack:** SO-101 and LeRobot turn the event into a concrete learning path rather than an abstract discussion of physical AI.

## How to engage

1. **Watch both task videos:** Identify the objects, each arm's role, and the visible completion condition before opening the implementation.
2. **Inspect the repository:** Follow its recorded training and deployment workflow; treat the team's reported experience as one project, not guaranteed performance.
3. **Contact public organizers:** Ask about future editions through the event page; do not travel based on the closed Helsinki listing.

lessons.name: RoboCup 2027 (Nuremberg)
lessons.summary: RoboCup 2027 is the robot competition announced for Nuremberg, where teams test autonomous systems in shared challenge environments.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

RoboCup 2027 is the robot competition announced for Nuremberg, where teams test autonomous systems in shared challenge environments.

![Official RoboCup 2027 logo for Nuremberg](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-robocup-2027-nuremberg.webp)
*Official RoboCup 2027 logo for Nuremberg. Source: [Publisher](https://2027.robocup.org), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Announced venue and dates:** The organizer lists Messe Nürnberg and 15–21 June 2027 for the world championship.
- **More than football:** RoboCup's major categories include RoboCupSoccer, RoboCupRescue, RoboCup@Home, and Smart Manufacturing League.
- **Autonomous behavior:** In robot soccer, machines must perceive the game and act; the interesting engineering is not a human remotely choosing every move.

> **Key idea:** A league's rules define the engineering problem; choose the league before choosing the robot you want to build.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Software analogy:** A competition league resembles a shared test protocol: different teams implement systems that face comparable tasks and constraints.
- **Worked selection:** Compare a soccer task with an @Home service task; list the sensors, decisions, and physical actions each would require.
- **Local stepping stone:** RoboCup German Open is a separate event worth studying for match footage, results, and team preparation before considering the world championship.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the trailer:** Use it to understand the championship's scope, then read the major-league descriptions rather than assuming every league uses humanoids.
2. **Inspect qualification rules:** Follow the chosen league's current technical requirements and entry process; world-championship participation is not an automatic visitor registration.
3. **Plan a narrow contribution:** A perception benchmark, simulation tool, or reproducible subsystem may be a better first student deliverable than an entire competition team.
